title: Installation
forbidden: The installation settings are for provider administrators. They apply to the whole server: {scope, select, organisation {your organisation} other {all tenants}}.
scoped: Your role in the provider team covers selected tenants only. The installation settings concern all tenants at once, so they are not available to you.

descriptions.server: How browsers reach this server and whether passkeys are offered. Applies to {scope, select, organisation {your organisation} other {all tenants}}.
descriptions.mail: The transport for reports, alerts and invitations. Used for {scope, select, organisation {your organisation} other {all tenants}}.
descriptions.microsoftApp: The app registration this installation uses to reach Microsoft 365.
descriptions.journal: The SMTP receiver for Exchange journal reports. One receiver serves {scope, select, organisation {your organisation} other {all tenants}}.
descriptions.defaultStorage: Where data is kept for {scope, select, organisation {your organisation} other {every tenant without a repository of its own}}.
descriptions.repository: Where data is kept for {scope, select, organisation {your organisation} other {every tenant without a repository of its own}}, and the network shares (NFS) a repository can point at.
descriptions.mounts: Network shares (NFS) used as backup storage.
descriptions.providerApi: Keys for RMM and PSA tools that work across all tenants.
descriptions.updates: Which version runs, which releases exist and how to update.
descriptions.edition: Which build runs and the switch to the full build.
descriptions.about: Version, source code and licenses of this installation.
descriptions.database: Where the database keeps its data, the free space of its disk and the repository's, and moving it to another disk.
descriptions.ransomware: How restore points are checked for signs of ransomware, and the thresholds of each signal, for {scope, select, organisation {your organisation} other {all tenants}}.

access.owner: You can look at these settings. Changing them needs the Owner role in the provider team.
access.administrator: You can look at this page. Running the test needs the Administrator role in the provider team or higher.
access.demo: This is a public demo. These settings are read-only here.

locked.title: {section} is not unlocked yet
locked.description: The section stays greyed out in the menu until it is unlocked. The page that unlocks it explains what is needed.

facts.title: This server
facts.note: The public URL decides the passkey domain, the redirect addresses for Microsoft sign-in and the address agents enrol against.

notice.title: Operator notice
notice.description: The responsibility notice accepted when this installation was set up. It is shown for reference and cannot be changed.
notice.acceptedNoDate: Accepted (version {version}). The date was not recorded.
notice.outdated: A newer version of the notice ({current}) is waiting to be accepted. A provider administrator is asked to read it when signing in.
notice.none: The notice has not been accepted yet.

microsoftApp.optional: Optional. This app is only needed when {scope, select, organisation {your organisation is connected by a consent link instead of its own app} other {tenants are connected by a consent link instead of their own app}}.

defaultStorage.loadError: The default repository could not be read.

card.title: Default repository
card.description: Where data is kept when {scope, select, organisation {your organisation has} other {a tenant has}} no repository of its own. It is set below or, without a saved setting, comes from the server environment.

usage.label: In use by
usage.none: No tenant. Each tenant has a repository of its own.
usage.organisationYes: Your organisation. It has no repository of its own.
usage.organisationNo: Nobody. Your organisation has a repository of its own.

misconfigured.title: The storage settings are invalid
misconfigured.description: STORAGE_TARGET, STORAGE_LOCAL_PATH or the S3_* values in the .env file of the server do not describe a usable repository. Correct them and restart {appName}, or save a default repository below.
misconfigured.savedTitle: The saved default repository cannot be used
misconfigured.savedDescription: The default repository saved on this page cannot be opened, for example because the master key changed. Save it again below.

insecure.title: The default repository uses plain HTTP
insecure.savedDescription: Access keys and backups travel unencrypted to the storage service. {appName} keeps using it, but saving it again requires an https:// endpoint. Switch the storage service to HTTPS and save the new endpoint below.
insecure.environmentDescription: S3_ENDPOINT in the .env file of the server starts with http://, so access keys and backups travel unencrypted. {appName} keeps using it. Switch the storage service to HTTPS, change S3_ENDPOINT to https:// and restart {appName}.

test.title: Test
test.description: Writes, reads, lists and deletes a small object on the default and checks whether it can lock objects. The test is logged.
test.passed: The last test passed {when}, run by {who}.
test.failed: The last test failed {when}, run by {who}.

errors.misconfigured: The storage settings in the environment are invalid, so there is nothing to test.
errors.environmentInvalid: The storage settings in the server environment are not usable, so the saved setting cannot be removed. Correct them first.
errors.unreachable: The location did not pass the test, so nothing was saved.
errors.inUse: Backups are kept in the current default repository, so it cannot point elsewhere yet.

source.label: Set in
source.database: Saved on this page by {who} on {when}

override.title: The setting saved here takes precedence
override.description: The server environment describes a default repository as well. It applies again once the setting saved here is removed:

configure.title: Change default repository
configure.description: A directory on the server or S3-compatible object storage, with the same settings as a repository. Before saving, a small test object is written, read, listed and deleted there; a location that fails is not saved. Access keys are stored encrypted and never shown again.

testHint.local: The directory must already exist on the server and be writable, for example a mounted volume or network share.
testHint.s3: Leave both key fields empty to keep the saved key pair. It is only used for the endpoint it was saved for.

configure.removeDescription: The setting saved here is removed and the default repository the server environment describes applies again. It is tested first:

blockers.title: {scope, select, organisation {Your organisation keeps backups on the current default} other {Tenants keep backups on the current default}}
blockers.description: Pointing the default elsewhere would leave these backups behind, so only changes that keep the location are possible: the key pair, the region or the addressing style. First give {scope, select, organisation {your organisation} other {each tenant listed}} a repository of its own under Repositories: replace the primary and move the existing backups, or add a copy and promote it once it is complete.

reasons.previous: older backups still live here after a replacement
reasons.migration: is being moved off it right now
reasons.active_job: a backup or another storage run is waiting or running

journal.loadError: The journal receiver could not be read.

receiver.title: Receiver
receiver.description: {appName} accepts Exchange Online journal reports on this port. The values come from the server environment and are read when the API starts.

checklist.title: What Exchange Online needs from this server

journal.perTenant: The journal address of each tenant, its rotation and the guide for Exchange Online are on the Archive page of that tenant.

providerApi.intro: Provider keys read across all tenants, for RMM and PSA tools. A key belongs to this installation, not to one tenant.

moved.title: Provider keys moved
moved.description: The keys that work across all tenants are under Installation, Provider API now. This page keeps the keys of the active tenant.

mounts.loadError: The mounts could not be loaded.
mounts.intro: Network shares (NFS) that {appName} uses as backup storage. Each network share appears in the api and the worker at {path}; a repository of the kind "directory" then points there.

unavailable.title: The mounter is not running
unavailable.description: Network shares are added by the mounter, an optional container next to {appName}. It is off by default. To use it, run this command once on the server:
unavailable.defaultDir: The command assumes the installer's default directory /opt/restow. If {appName} is installed in another directory, use that one instead.

composeOutdated.title: The compose file has no mounter
composeOutdated.description: The docker-compose.yml of this installation was written before the mounter existed, and updates do not replace it. Run the installer again on the server: it replaces the file with the one of the installed release and keeps the previous one as a backup next to it. .env stays as it is.
composeOutdated.then: Then start the mounter with the command below.

unavailable.security: The mounter has access to the Docker socket, which amounts to root access on the host. Read the documentation on network shares before you enable it.

reason.disabled: The connection to the mounter is switched off on this server.
reason.no_secret: The mounter has not started yet, or its shared secret is not readable.
reason.unreachable: Nothing answers at the mounter's address.
reason.timeout: The mounter did not answer in time.
reason.incompatible: The mounter answered in a format this version does not understand. Recreate it with the image of this version.

unavailable.demo: Network shares cannot be added in the demo.

enable.description: The updater can start the mounter for you. The mounter mounts the Docker socket, which amounts to root access on the host.
enable.starting: The mounter is starting. This page updates as soon as it answers.
enable.started: The updater started the mounter {when}. If it does not answer within a minute, look at its log: docker compose logs mounter
enable.orCommand: Or run this command on the host, in the directory that holds docker-compose.yml:
enable.disable: Switching it off stays a command on the host ({command}); runs of file shares in progress then fail.

failed.title: The updater could not start the mounter
failed.compose_unsupported: The docker-compose.yml of this installation has no mounter service that takes its image from RESTOW_MOUNTER_IMAGE. Use the docker-compose.yml of this release.
failed.env_write_failed: The updater could not write RESTOW_MOUNTER_IMAGE into .env.
failed.launch_failed: The updater could not start its helper container.
failed.helper_failed: docker compose up of the mounter failed.
failed.interrupted: The updater stopped while it started the mounter.

list.title: Network shares
list.description: Network shares that are mounted into the api and the worker.
list.storageHint: To keep backups on a network share, add a repository of the kind "directory" with the network share's path, or a folder below it.

blockers.title: Network shares cannot be changed right now
blockers.docker_cli_missing: The mounter is still preparing its Docker tools. Try again in a minute.
blockers.compose_missing: The mounter finds no compose file in the project directory.
blockers.compose_file_variable: COMPOSE_FILE is set in .env. Docker Compose would then not read the override file the network shares are written to.
blockers.override_invalid: The compose override file cannot be read. Correct it by hand first.

status.rolled_back: Failed, the previous state was restored

operation.restart: The api and the worker restart during this step. This page may not respond for a moment.
operation.needsAttention: The previous state could not be restored automatically. Check docker-compose.override.yml in the project directory and run docker compose up -d. The documentation on mounts describes the steps.
operation.dismissHint: The next change replaces this report.

steps.apply: Restart the api and the worker

validate.exists: A network share with this name exists already.
validate.not_found: There is no network share with this name.
validate.conflict: The compose override already mounts something at this path.
validate.limit: The maximum number of network shares is reached.

prepare.compose_missing: No compose file was found in the project directory.

probe.mount_failed: The network share could not be mounted. Check the server address, the export path, the NFS version and whether the server exports the path to this host.
probe.export_not_found: The export path {export} does not exist on {server}.
probe.not_writable: The network share was mounted but is not writable. Check the permissions on the server (root squash maps root to an unprivileged user).
probe.timeout: The server did not answer in time.
probe.failed: The test of the network share failed.

write.invalid_override: The compose override file cannot be changed.
write.failed: The compose override file could not be written.
write.config_invalid: Docker Compose did not accept the new configuration.

apply.failed: The api and the worker could not be restarted with the network share.

health.timeout: The api or the worker did not become ready in time.
health.crashed: The api or the worker stopped after the restart.

failures.interrupted: The mounter stopped while the change was running.

exportNotFound.showmount: The server answered but has no export with this path. Check the exact path it exports with:
exportNotFound.synology: On a Synology NAS the path starts with the volume, for example /volume1{path}.
exportNotFound.nfsVersion: With NFSv4 some servers show their exports below a pseudo-root, with different paths. Try NFS version 3.

dialog.title: Add an NFS network share
dialog.description: The network share is tested first. Adding it restarts the api and the worker, which takes a moment.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.nameHint: 1 to 32 characters: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. The network share appears at {path}.
dialog.serverHint: Host name, IPv4 or IPv6 address of the NFS server.
dialog.exportHint: The path the server exports, for example /volume1/backup.
dialog.readOnlyHint: Mount the network share read-only. Backups cannot be written to it.

invalid.name: Use 1 to 32 characters: a-z, 0-9 and hyphens, not at the start or end.
invalid.server: Enter a host name or an IP address, without commas, spaces or "=".
invalid.export: Enter an absolute path, without commas, spaces, ":", "=" or "..".

test.ok: The network share is reachable and writable.
test.okReadOnly: The network share is reachable and readable.

remove.title: Remove the network share {name}?
remove.description: The network share is unmounted from the api and the worker, which restart. The data on the server is not touched.
remove.inUse: The network share is still used by these repositories:

toast.adding: The network share is being added.
toast.removing: The network share is being removed.

errors.jobsRunning: Backups or restores are running. Changing a network share restarts the api and the worker; try again when they have finished.
errors.inUse: The network share is still used by a repository.
errors.demo: Network shares cannot be changed in the demo.

rejected.busy: Another change to the network shares is running.
rejected.blocked: The mounter cannot change network shares right now.
rejected.exists: A network share with this name exists already.
rejected.not_found: There is no network share with this name.
rejected.conflict: The compose override already mounts something at this path.
rejected.limit: The maximum number of network shares is reached.
rejected.invalid_request: The mounter did not accept the settings.

errors.pendingExists: Another network share is already waiting for running jobs to finish. Cancel it under Installation > Network shares first.
errors.pendingNotFound: This network share is no longer waiting.
errors.enableUnavailable: The mounter cannot be started from here: the updater does not run. Run the command on the host.
errors.enableRefused: The updater cannot start the mounter right now (an update is scheduled or running). Try again when it has finished.

pending.title: The network share {name} waits for running jobs
pending.description: Backups or restores are running. {appName} adds the network share as soon as they have finished. Requested by {who}, {when}.
pending.failedTitle: The waiting network share {name} could not be added

storageOffer.detected: This is the address of an NFS network share:
storageOffer.existing: This network share is mounted already as {name}.
storageOffer.askOwner: Only the owner of the provider team can mount network shares. Ask the provider owner to mount this network share under Installation > Network shares: server {server}, export path {export}, NFS 4.1, read-write. Its path then appears below this field.
storageOffer.description: {appName} can mount it read-write through the mounter and fill in its path for you.
storageOffer.invalidSubfolder: Enter a relative folder, without commas, spaces, ":", "=" or "..".
storageOffer.restart: {appName} restarts its api and worker once (a few seconds); the page reconnects by itself.
storageOffer.blocked: Network shares cannot be changed right now: another change is running or the mounter is not ready. See Installation > Network shares.
storageOffer.waitingTitle: Waiting for running jobs to finish
storageOffer.starting: The network share is being mounted ...
storageOffer.done: The network share {name} is mounted and its path was filled in. Save the repository to use it.

database.loadError: The database information could not be loaded.
database.intro: Where the database keeps its data, how much room its disk and the disk of the local repository have, and moving the database to another disk.

location.title: Database location
location.description: The database holds the catalogue of every backup. When its disk runs full, the database stops.

disks.repository: Disk under the local default repository
disks.lowBody: Less than a tenth of the disk is free (and less than 5 GiB). A full disk stops the database or the backups. Free up space, enlarge the disk, or move the database to another disk below. Provider administrators are notified once in the bell and through alert rules with “Low disk space”.

updateSpace.title: Space for the next update
updateSpace.enough: The next update needs about {needed} (backup of the database {dump}, new images {images}, room for migrations {migrations}); {free} are free.
updateSpace.short: The next update needs about {needed} (backup of the database {dump}, new images {images}, room for migrations {migrations}), but only {free} are free. The updater refuses the update until there is room.

updater.ready: The location of the database could not be read. Is the database running?
updater.unsupported: The updater predates this function. It is replaced with the next update; until then the database can only be moved by hand (docs/DATABASE.md).
updater.unavailable: The optional updater does not answer. Without it the location cannot be read or changed here; the steps by hand are in docs/DATABASE.md.
updater.demo: The demonstration installation does not change its database.

form.title: Move the database to another disk
form.description: Enter a directory on the host, for example the mount point of an attached volume. {appName} checks it first; nothing changes until you confirm the move.
form.directoryHint: An absolute path on another local disk (ext4, XFS, Btrfs or ZFS; no network drive). {appName} creates a subdirectory restow-postgres-<time> in it.
form.manual: To move the database by hand, follow docs/DATABASE.md, “Moving by hand”.
form.notMovable: The docker-compose.yml of this installation does not read the database location from .env. Use the docker-compose.yml of this release (for example by running the installer again), then the database can be moved here.
form.updateActive: An update is announced or running. Move the database after it.

check.facts: File system {filesystem}, {free} free, {needed} needed (the database and a margin).
check.failed: The database cannot be moved to this directory:

problems.path_invalid: The path is not a valid directory for the database: an absolute path of letters, digits and . _ - + @, not a system directory.
problems.path_missing: The directory does not exist on the host, or it is not a directory. Create it (on the mounted disk) and check again.
problems.not_writable: The directory cannot be written to.
problems.same_filesystem: The directory is on the same disk as the database now. Choose a directory on another disk.
problems.filesystem_unsuitable: The file system is not suitable for the database. It needs a local file system (ext4, XFS, Btrfs or ZFS), not a network drive (NFS, SMB) or a memory file system.
problems.insufficient_space: There is not enough free space for the database and a margin.
problems.tablespaces: The database uses tablespaces outside its directory; it cannot be moved here.
problems.compose_unsupported: The docker-compose.yml does not read the database location from .env. Use the docker-compose.yml of this release.
problems.location_unknown: The current location or size of the database could not be read. Is the database running?
problems.env_unwritable: The updater cannot write the .env file.
problems.busy: An update, a restart or another move is running. Try again afterwards.
problems.unknown: The updater reported a problem this version does not know.

errors.busy: An update, a restart or another move is running. Try again afterwards.
errors.unsupported: The updater predates this function. It is replaced with the next update.

confirm.title: Move the database?
confirm.description: The database ({size}) is copied to the new directory, checked and switched over. To confirm, type the directory below.
confirm.downtime: {appName} is unavailable during the move: the copy and its check read the data about three times. Plan for several minutes per 10 GB.
confirm.jobs: Running backups are interrupted and continue after the move.
confirm.rollback: If a step fails, {appName} starts again from the current location, unchanged.
confirm.keep: The current copy is kept until you remove it.

move.title: Database move
move.downtime: {appName} is stopped while the database moves. This page follows the move; it continues by itself when {appName} is back.
move.away: {appName} is stopped for the move and does not answer right now. This page waits and shows the result when it is back.
move.succeeded: The database now runs from {to}. The copy was checked file by file ({entries} entries) and in a test start before the switch.
move.rolledBack: {appName} went back to the old location; the database there is unchanged.
move.needsAttention: The way back did not complete either. {appName} may be stopped. Follow docs/DATABASE.md, “When a move needs attention”.
move.keptCopy: The copy in {path} is kept because the database already ran from it. Remove it by hand once you no longer need it.

steps.verify: Compare the copy with the original
steps.trial: Test start of the database on the copy
steps.start_database: Start the database from the new directory

stop_application.failed: The application could not be stopped.

stop_database.failed: The database could not be stopped.
stop_database.unclean: The database did not shut down cleanly.

verify.mismatch: The copy differs from the original.
verify.failed: The copy could not be compared with the original.

trial.failed: The database did not start on the copy.
trial.mismatch: The copy does not hold the same database as the original.

switch.compose_unsupported: The docker-compose.yml does not read the database location from .env.
switch.failed: Switching to the new directory failed.

start_database.failed: The database did not start from the new directory.
start_database.wrong_location: The database started, but not from the new directory.

start_application.failed: The application did not start after the move.

failure.interrupted: The updater stopped while the move was running.
failure.unknown: The move failed for a reason this version does not know.

oldCopies.title: Old copy of the database
oldCopies.description: The previous location is kept after a move and cannot be started by mistake. Remove it once the database runs well from the new disk; this frees its space.
oldCopies.confirmDescription: The content of {location} is deleted. Only a note file stays, so the directory cannot be mistaken for an empty database. This cannot be undone.
